payload.claim: None of the three new second-ask tests (`test_a_survivor_the_whole_suite_kills_stays_a_blocker_naming_the_killing_tests`, `test_a_survivor_the_whole_suite_also_misses_says_the_suite_stayed_green`, `test_a_survivor_whose_whole_suite_cannot_answer_keeps_todays_blocker`) ever assert `probe_verdict` on the blockers they read from `rebuttal.json`. REBUT's own `_blocker_line` (saffron/phases/rebut.py:178) only shows the implementer the missed edit when `f.probe_verdict == "survived"`, so this field is exactly what decides whether the probe is disclosed. In `saffron/cell/session.py:2117-2123`, adding `"probe_verdict": suite_result.verdict` to the `model_copy` update (a very plausible edit, since `suite_result.verdict` is the same `Verdict` type the field already holds) would silently set `probe_verdict` to `"killed"` or `"unproven"` for every survivor that reaches the second ask, suppressing the probe line REBUT shows the implementer for exactly the new code path this PR adds — while every assertion in these three tests (severity, filed_severity, claim text, probe, subsets, cell.mutated) still passes.
